lines.text: human history offers us the picture of a humanity which is
not as it should be and might be, but instead is disfigured
and defaced.
Not readiness for the future, but fear of it, is the decisive
motivating force in human life. Really to live availably for
the future would mean to overcome the anguished fear of it
in the certainty that whatever it brings can only serve our
ultimate good. And the final proof of the Christian attitude
would be not to shudder and recoil at the thought of the
death which the future will assuredly bring to every one of
us, but rather to go forward to meet it undismayed in the
assured conviction that "neither death nor life, nor angels
nor principalities, nor things present nor things to come, nor
powers... Will be able to separate us from the love of God".
But who can speak with this degree of assurance? May
perhaps he whose aims are not tangible worldly goods, but
who strives only to attain the purity and perfection of his
own true being? Does not such a one live with a view to a
genuine future? Does he not look to a future which can rob
him of nothing since he has not set his heart on transitory
and tangible things? No doubt he lives by the inspiration of
what he wishes to become, yet not in view of the real future
which is coming to him. He is living in the strength of his
own resources, not by the blessing which the future will
bring to him and not in readiness for the purposes which
God has for him. But the more he lives by his own strength,
the more also he lives enslaved to the past, to what he has
made of himself. And the more frankly he confesses that he is
not yet what he wishes to become, the more he becomes
conscious of the discord in which his life is rooted; he would
like to be the man whom he sees before him as a serene and
shining ideal, and yet he is ever entrapped by his own past
with its half-heartedness and pettiness, its impurity and evil
from which he can never free himself. And then his hope
cleaves no longer to what he wishes to make of himself, but
to the possibility of release and redemption from the fetters
of self, and the basic disharmony of his being. He is not
